345545.title: The growth constant for the stack-sorting map
345545.source_name: Colin Defant and James Propp, “Quantifying Noninvertibility in Discrete Dynamical Systems”, arXiv:2002.07144 (2020).
345545.history_check: Grep of campaign 2026-10-27 md/results/dispositions/ledger files for the ID and arXiv number: no prior technical entry for this ID (only same-source different-ID entries and the r133 launch note).
345545.review_depth: Primary v4 Definition 1.1, Section 2.3, Theorem 2.5 with full proof, Section 4 Conjecture 4.4 and its evidence read; all four arXiv versions listed; Defant Troupes v2 Theorem 7.29 and Remark 7.30 read; Defant 2003.05935v2 grepped; Zhang 2606.24110 and Fried 2204.07873 screened.
345545.summary: Source deg = (1/n!) sum_y |s^-1(y)|^2 (average fiber multiplicity; the MathDB "maximum fiber size" paraphrase is a defect: the literal maximum gives limit 4). New exact formula: the closure of two postorder tree orders is a postorder forest, so by the hook-length formula d_n = sum over pairs of tree shapes of prod 1/h_j. A block recursion makes P_n = n! d_n polynomial-time. Exact P_50 with the doubling form of source inequality (1) gives lim d_n^(1/n) >= 1.7330 > 1.73. Independently, P_78 with the source sup formula gives > 1.7319. So Conjecture 4.4 is false. Extrapolated limit approx 1.9532.
345545.mechanism: Exact integer certificate P_50 (also P_78) plus the source Fekete argument; the DP is proved in candidate-345545/CANDIDATE.md section 3.3.
345545.verification: DP equals brute force for n<=10; an independent automaton DP equals it for n<=14; shape-pair closure equals brute force for n<=6; exact integer inequalities checked.
345545.lean_status: UNCOMPILED draft candidate-345545/lean/StackSortDegree.lean (endpoint plus lemma chain with sorry placeholders). Lean cost medium-high: DP correctness (trees, closure, forest hook formula, blocks) dominates.
345545.significance: Refutes a published conjecture (EJC 2020) that Defant restated as open in 2022 after reaching a 1.62924 lower bound. The new polynomial formula is the key; the conjecture fails by a wide margin.
345545.prior_art: Web searches 2026-11-03 found no later bound or refutation; OEIS-style search for 1,4,26,224,2356,29064 found nothing; registry path screens clear (Omega c7f3e33e D5 and Problems; OpenAI preprints listing at 4eaee875).

358865.title: The density conjecture for distance-restricted firefighting on square grids
358865.source_name: Andrea C. Burgess, John Hawkin, Alexander Howse, John Marcoux and David A. Pike, “Distance-Restricted Firefighting on Finite Graphs”, arXiv:2306.12575 (2025).
358865.history_check: Grep of campaign 2026-10-27 md/results/dispositions/ledger files for the ID and arXiv number: no prior technical entry for this ID (only same-source different-ID entries and the r133 launch note).
358865.review_depth: Primary v3 Section 1 definitions, Lemma 3.1 with proof and Conjecture 3.2 read.
358865.summary: Lower bound n^2/8 is the source Lemma 3.1. Under the source rules the firefighter moves at most 1 step per turn and protects its vertex, so walls are 4-connected walks racing an L1 fire. In the continuum family (inward leg meeting the front, then an outward monotone leg), area 2b(n/2-b) is maximised at b=n/4, giving exactly n^2/8. This supports the conjecture, but a proof must control arbitrary walk strategies; no finite certificate is possible for a limit statement.
